auditor_findings: CONFIRMED live defect (Finding B1): the committed out/chatgpt-project-upload-set/TP-DMX-FDOS-004-....zip does NOT contain PACKAGE_VALIDATION.json (verified via `unzip -l`), even though the package's own README.md line 11 explicitly lists it as a deliverable. Root cause: build_chatgpt_project_sources.py's build_zip_archive() (called from main() at line 488) runs and finalizes the ZIP before validate_chatgpt_project_sources.py ever executes as a separate script to produce that file, and no committed step rebuilds the ZIP afterward. This was flagged by chatgpt-codex-connector in a review thread posted ~4 minutes after the R1 repair commit (94c1dcb1bc) landed -- i.e. against the exact head under audit, not a stale prior head -- and does not appear in PROOF.json's residual-risk disclosure. Does not affect the 40 UPLOAD_FILES/ themselves (the actual ChatGPT-Project upload content), only the bundled audit trail.

NEW bug found independently by this audit (Finding A): build_zip_archive() crashes with an uncaught ValueError (`zip_path.relative_to(repo_root)`) whenever --output-dir resolves outside --repo-root -- reproduced directly with --output-dir /tmp/audit-rebuild. Harmless for the packet's own in-repo workflow (out/chatgpt-project-upload-set/), but breaks the natural 'rebuild into an external scratch dir to verify' pattern that any auditor or CI job would use.

Two additional post-repair chatgpt-codex-connector review threads (both timestamped ~4 min after 94c1dcb1bc, neither in PROOF.json's disclosure) describe real but currently-dormant structural gaps: (B2) build script line 191-192 trusts a self-reported `capture_complete` flag instead of always recomputing len(files)==changedFiles -- no live mismatch exists in the current 29 captured PRs (only #1123 is incomplete and correctly discloses capture_complete=false), but the fail-closed guard could be silently bypassed by a future bad capture; (B3) the material-PR classification filter (lines 231, 387) has no enum/allow-list validation, so a typo'd classification value would silently be treated as non-material rather than fail closed -- all 29 current values are valid, so no live occurrence today.

All 5 originally-flagged validator/assembler gaps (sidecar path, manifest-disk set-equality, hash-gate slot 38/40 skip, truncated open-PR capture handling, missing ZIP generation in the committed assembler) and the CI-red root causes (docs frontmatter, embedded_audit schema shape) are genuinely fixed -- independently re-verified via corruption tests, byte-diffed rebuilds, and live gh queries, not by trusting PROOF.json's narrative.
fixes_applied_from_audit: Finding A: build_zip_archive() now catches the ValueError from zip_path.relative_to(repo_root) and falls back to a bare basename in the sidecar for out-of-repo output dirs. Independent verifier: built into /tmp/verify-a/pkg (outside repo root) -- exit 0, both pkg.zip and pkg.zip.sha256 produced, `shasum -a 256 -c` passed.

Finding B1: validate_chatgpt_project_sources.py was refactored to expose a run_validation() function; build_chatgpt_project_sources.py's main() now calls it and writes PACKAGE_VALIDATION.json into the output dir BEFORE build_zip_archive() runs (and fails closed via SystemExit if any gate fails), so the file is genuinely inside the shipped ZIP. Independent verifier: `unzip -l` on the freshly-built ZIP shows PACKAGE_VALIDATION.json present, contents show all_gates_pass:true.

Finding B2: build_pr_ledger_entries() no longer trusts a self-reported capture_complete field -- it is now always recomputed as len(files) == pr.get('changedFiles', -1). Independent verifier: fed the real function a forged PR record with capture_complete=True self-reported but an actual file-count mismatch; it ignored the lie and raised the FATAL incomplete-capture error, proving the self-reported flag has no effect.

Finding B3: added a VALID_PR_CLASSIFICATIONS enum and a fail-closed check in build_pr_ledger_entries() that raises SystemExit if any classification value isn't a recognized member. Independent verifier: ran the build with a scratch pr_classifications.json containing a bogus classification value for one PR -- script exited 1 with a FATAL error naming the exact PR and bad value.
